status: candidate; semantic construction studies, not aesthetic validation

operations.relation: Several contributions jointly affect the same result
operations.operation: Distinct continuous marks extend across one shared result surface
asserts: Each depicted contribution acts across that surface
operations.useWhen: The brief supports joint influence across the represented result, rather than assigning its parts to separate contributors.
operations.failure: A set of adjacent owned stripes, or marks ending at different result fields, can imply exclusive responsibility. Do not add field-wise effects that the facts do not support.
operations.adapt: Marks can become traces, transparent planes or aligned interventions. Preserve the common object; change their material and spacing for the selected style.

operations.relation: Several inputs reach the same receiver
operations.operation: Independent paths enter one shared receiver
operations.useWhen: Combining inputs or sharing a destination is the intended meaning. It may be insufficient when collaboration itself must be explained.
operations.failure: Calling an ordinary fork-in 'collaboration' adds meaning that its geometry does not communicate.
operations.adapt: Keep the destination unambiguous. Vary direction, line character and receiver material rather than inventing different input roles.

operations.relation: One requirement applies throughout several activities
operations.operation: A quiet common field extends beneath all affected activities
asserts: Shared scope over the enclosed activities
operations.useWhen: An obligation, operating condition or judgement applies to multiple activities.
operations.failure: Moving the field into a separate final box turns scope into a last stage; a dominant field can drown out the activity being explained.
operations.adapt: Use an enclosure, substrate or repeated edge treatment when a fill conflicts with the work. Keep the scope label outside activity labels.

operations.relation: A proposal selects one or more routes before shared checking and delivery
operations.operation: Split into alternatives, rejoin, then enter the common check
doesNotAssert: Checking is an alternative production route
operations.useWhen: The brief explicitly allows selection or combination and names a common downstream stage.
operations.failure: Putting the check on the branching spine makes it a sibling option instead of a shared consequence. Use words to distinguish one-of from combinable choices.
operations.adapt: Change route count and route labels from facts. Preserve the split and the later join; do not infer an execution schedule from alignment.

operations.relation: An outcome updates a resource that informs later decisions
operations.operation: A subordinate return lands on the resource being changed
asserts: The updated resource supports a later decision
doesNotAssert: An extra step in every present execution
An update to an unrelated adjacent object
operations.useWhen: Feedback has a named destination, such as a method library, model, dataset or prior decision.
operations.failure: A neat loop into an arbitrary corner hides what changes. An oversized return competes with the main path.
operations.adapt: Keep the target object and arrow endpoint explicit; use a lighter return corridor when the current task is the main story.

operations.operation: Successive objects share a readable directional axis
operations.useWhen: The main relationship is genuinely an ordinary ordered process. This is the direct route, not a failure of originality.
operations.failure: An elaborate metaphor can obscure a simple process. Equal spacing is not a time scale.
operations.adapt: Use steps, a continuous track or ordinary nodes and edges as appropriate. Retain any supplied branches and exceptions.

operations.relation: A condition changes a property of the same object
operations.operation: Corresponding views preserve identity, scale and position while only the stated feature changes
asserts: The marked feature is the stated change
operations.useWhen: A before/after, controlled comparison or mechanism needs the unchanged substrate to stay recognizable.
operations.failure: Redrawing the whole object introduces accidental differences, and decorative bars can look like fabricated measurements.
operations.adapt: Use real supplied data for quantitative comparisons. For conceptual diagrams, keep changes schematic and explicitly labelled.
